strengths: Well-motivated biological insight that perturbation responses are coordinated at the program level rather than gene-wise; effectively demonstrated in Figure 1
Comprehensive experimental validation across two benchmarks with rigorous comparison against 13 strong baselines and multiple evaluation metrics (ρ∆, ρ∆D, ACC∆, ACC∆D, DES, PDS, L2, MSE, MAE)
Particularly strong results on out-of-distribution generalization tasks (e.g., 38.0% improvement over CellFlow on ρ∆D for unseen single perturbations in holdout setting)
Thorough ablation studies (Tables 4a-4e) systematically validate each component and demonstrate their synergistic contributions
Biological validation through pathway enrichment analysis (Figures 8-9) and mechanistic case studies (Figure 4) confirm discovered modules align with known biological pathways
Excellent reproducibility: detailed algorithms (1-3), comprehensive implementation details in appendix (A.3), low standard deviations across seeds (Tables 7-8), and code in supplementary materials
Clean, modular framework design with clear three-stage architecture; well-presented with informative figures and logical flow
Robustness analysis demonstrating stable results across multiple random seeds and datasets
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: GRC uses standard balanced assignment via optimal transport; GCAE is incremental Perceiver-style bottleneck; conditional flow matching borrowed from concurrent work (Klein et al. 2025); biological losses are established techniques. Contribution is primarily in combination rather than fundamental innovation

Static module induction may miss context-specific regulatory rewiring: GRC partitions genes offline independent of perturbation condition or cell state; no analysis of module stability across different perturbations; authors acknowledge this limitation (§A.6) but it's a significant biological assumption

Heavy dependence on external priors (GeneCompass embeddings, STRING PPI at threshold 700, Reactome pathways) with limited robustness analysis; performance would degrade with poor embeddings or incomplete databases; Table 4e shows embedding sensitivity
Balanced cluster size constraint (uniform |c_k| = G/K) enforces artificial homogeneity potentially misaligned with true biological program distributions; no validation this reflects reality

Evaluation limited to two mammalian cell line datasets (K562, RPE1) with CRISPR perturbations; no cross-dataset generalization, evaluation on other perturbation modalities, or assessment on diverse cell types; limits generalizability claims

Modest improvements on several key metrics: 7.7% over CellFlow on ρ∆ (Table 1) and 5.9% on DES; improvements on RPE1 less compelling as baselines are weaker overall; unclear if gains justify method complexity

GRC optimization lacks convergence analysis: alternating Sinkhorn + rounding solved offline without analysis of convergence properties, local minima, or initialization sensitivity; number of iterations T unspecified
Incomplete technical details: tie-breaking in arg max assignment, Stage 1 convergence criterion, pathway activation computation in Eq. 8, handling of genes absent from PPI/pathway databases
Method complexity with five key components and numerous hyperparameters (λ_corr, λ_pathway, K, M, etc.) may hinder adoption; limited guidance on hyperparameter setting for new datasets
Interpretability analysis limited to qualitative case studies (Fig. 4) on two perturbations; no systematic analysis of which modules drive predictions or statistical validation of attention patterns

strengths: Well-motivated biological problem: the observation that perturbation responses manifest as coordinated program-level changes is sensible and addresses a real gap in existing generative models.

Comprehensive experimental evaluation with multiple evaluation splits (additive/holdout), diverse metrics (point-prediction and biological fidelity), extensive ablations (Table 4), and robustness analysis across seeds.
Strong empirical results on challenging settings, particularly for unseen combinatorial perturbations (28.6% improvement in ρ∆D and 15.4% in ACC∆D on Norman holdout double-gene task).
Solid biological validation: pathway enrichment analysis (Figures 8-9) convincingly demonstrates that GRC discovers functionally coherent modules corresponding to real biological processes.
Mechanistic interpretability via attention visualization and clear technical exposition with comprehensive implementation details, algorithms, and hyperparameter specifications.
Good reproducibility practices: code provided, detailed hyperparameters (Table 9), low standard deviations across seeds (Tables 7-8), and honest discussion of limitations (§A.6).
weaknesses: Core claim inadequately isolated: the paper claims to be first to explicitly model module-level induction for perturbation prediction, but improvements could plausibly arise from superior encoder architecture (GCAE with Perceiver bottleneck), better flow matching implementation, or improved loss design rather than module structure per se. Critically, there is no ablation that completely removes module structure to quantify its isolated contribution.

Fundamental contradiction in motivation and execution: the paper critiques static biological priors as insufficient, yet heavily relies on static PPI networks (STRING at threshold 700), static pathway annotations (Reactome), static gene embeddings (GeneCompass), and static offline clustering (GRC is computed once, never adapting). The claim of 'context-adaptive module induction' is unsupported.

Module quality validation is retrospective and partially circular: pathway enrichment validates that discovered clusters are coherent with Reactome annotations, but (1) this doesn't prove clusters outperform alternatives (random, K-means, GO-based) for prediction, (2) employing Reactome in the loss function while validating on Reactome creates circular reasoning about biological validity.

Modest improvements relative to substantially added complexity: ~7.7% on Norman additive (primary benchmark) and 3.1% on ρ∆D despite introducing GRC clustering, Perceiver bottleneck, dual loss terms, two-stage training, and dependencies on multiple pretrained models and databases. The cost-benefit analysis is unfavorable.

Limited evaluation scope severely constrains generalizability: only two cell types (K562 and RPE1) from CRISPR perturbations tested. Unknown generalization to chemical perturbations, multi-omics, diverse cell types, or alternative organisms. Larger improvements on RPE1 (25.7% ρ∆) may reflect higher baseline difficulty rather than principled advantage.

Circular evaluation design: GRC uses PPI to cluster genes, the model operates on these clusters, and biological fidelity is measured by alignment with the same pathway databases (Reactome) constraining the model via Lpathway. This conflates model alignment with known priors with genuine biological validity.

Insufficient justification of design choices: (1) K=32 clusters has no principled derivation; (2) λcorr=λpathway=0.1 is symmetric without justification; (3) cost matrix (Eq. 1) uses simple sum D_sem+D_PPI without exploring alternatives or weighting schemes; (4) GRC's alternating optimization convergence properties are not discussed.

Foundation model dependency under-explored: Table 4e shows GeneCompass better for clustering but ESM2 better for conditioning—a reversal that is concerning and inadequately explained. This raises questions about whether success is robust to embedding choice or contingent on specific models.

Missing critical ablations: no variant completely removing module structure, no comparison of GRC-discovered clusters to alternatives (K-means, GO-based), no isolated test of whether GCAE bottleneck (vs. flat architecture) drives improvements, no systematic failure case analysis.

Limited mechanistic understanding: Figure 4 provides attention visualizations for only two perturbations without systematic analysis of when module-based modeling helps or fails. No analysis of perturbation classes or conditions under which scBIG underperforms.

strengths: Well-motivated module-level inductive bias addressing a real limitation in existing perturbation models—coordinated gene programs neglected by gene-wise approaches

Comprehensive technical framework with principled design: GRC integrates semantic and PPI priors via optimal transport; GCAE captures inter-module dependencies via Perceiver bottleneck; structure-aware losses preserve biological coherence
Rigorous experimental validation with consistent improvements (6.7% average, 38% on challenging ρ∆^D metric) across two benchmarks and multiple evaluation settings (additive/holdout splits)

Thorough ablation studies (Tables 4a-e) systematically validating each component; particularly insightful: GRC outperforms k-means (5.2%), complementary biological losses (3.1% joint gain), different embedding roles

Strong biological validation: pathway enrichment confirms functional coherence of induced modules; mechanistic attention shift analysis (Fig. 4) aligns with known regulatory relationships (NOL8→mTORC1, KCTD10→G2/M)
Excellent reproducibility: code provided, comprehensive implementation details (Algorithms 1-3), standard deviations across 5 seeds, clear hyperparameter documentation
Particularly strong performance on unseen/combinatorial perturbations (38% improvement ρ∆^D, 35.9% improvement DES on Norman holdout), directly addressing important generalization challenge
Clear presentation with informative Figure 2 overview; methods logically organized
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: individual components (OT clustering, Perceiver, flow matching) are established; novelty is primarily in architectural combination rather than fundamental methodological innovation

Heavy dependence on external priors (GeneCompass embeddings, STRING PPI, Reactome pathways) creates brittleness; no robustness analysis with degraded/noisy priors; performance is prior-quality dependent

Static module induction is foundational limitation: fixed K=32 across all datasets; no context-adaptive reorganization of modules across cell states or perturbation regimes; acknowledged but unresolved

Evaluation scope narrower than generalizability claims suggest: only 2 datasets (Norman K562 CRISPRa + RPE1 CRISPRi), only 2 cell lines, only CRISPR perturbations; no cross-cell-type, cross-species, or chemical perturbation evaluation; 'zero-shot' is within-protocol only
Improvements uneven across metrics and datasets: RPE1 shows +25.7% ρ∆ but only +5.6% L2; some single-digit gains vs. strong baselines; improvements solid but not exceptional

Inference procedure for truly unseen perturbations not clearly specified: precomputation of R*_gt and y*_gt targets (Algorithm 3 lines 5-6) unclear—does this require observed similar perturbations during training? Critical detail buried
Incomplete computational characterization: Table 5 shows per-step overhead but missing total training time, inference time, memory comparisons vs. baselines; practitioners need full picture
Limited failure mode analysis: no discussion of when/why scBIG underperforms; no error analysis showing which gene programs or perturbations are problematic

Some design choices lack justification: PPI threshold of 700 in STRING (why this value?), 20-gene DEG metrics (arbitrary?), λ_corr = λ_pathway = 0.1 (how selected?), M=8 inducing points (why optimal?)

Module quality validation could be deeper: pathway enrichment is statistical, not biological validation; only 2 attention shift case studies; unclear if modules capture canonical biological program hierarchies

strengths: Well-motivated biological insight addressing genuine limitation of gene-wise modeling in prior work
Technically solid framework integrating GRC, GCAE, and structure-aware objectives in principled manner
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple datasets (Norman, RPE1, ComboSciPlex), metrics, and evaluation settings (additive/holdout splits)
Strong and consistent empirical results with 6.7% average improvement, particularly pronounced on OOD generalization (38% on unseen single genes)
Thorough ablation studies (Tables 6a-6e) isolating contributions of individual components and design choices
Robust statistical validation including paired Wilcoxon tests and analysis across random seeds with low variance
Clear presentation with effective figures and extensive supplementary material including full algorithms, hyperparameters, and implementation details
Honest discussion of limitations (A.8) and acknowledgment of dependencies on external priors
Functional enrichment analysis (Figure 3) validates that induced clusters are biologically coherent
Promising results on cross-cell-line transfer and drug perturbations suggesting generalization beyond single dataset
weaknesses: Static module structure cannot adapt to perturbation context; biological programs likely reorganize under different conditions but scBIG partitions remain fixed
Balanced cluster size constraint (|c_k|=G/K) justified as 'architectural regularizer' but may not reflect biological reality where modules should have varying sizes

Heavy dependence on external resources (GeneCompass embeddings, STRING PPI at threshold 700, Reactome pathways) creates brittleness and limits generalization to new organisms/domains where priors incomplete

Limited biological validation: enrichment analysis is post-hoc, perturbation-specific coordination (Table 5) shown only for 3 examples, attention analysis (Figure 4) qualitative with 2 anecdotal cases, no wet-lab validation
Evaluation scope primarily focused on two human cell types (K562 dominant, RPE1); cross-cell-line transfer (Table 18) shows modest improvements suggesting cell-type specificity of modules
Mini-batch OT for pairing control/perturbed cells lacks justification; sensitivity to this choice not analyzed
Linear interpolation path assumption (zt=(1-t)z0+tz1) in flow matching may miss complex dynamics; no analysis of when linearity breaks down
Reconstruction loss (Eq. 5) abandoned after pretraining stage; joint optimization during fine-tuning not explored
Incremental architectural contributions: GCAE is standard Perceiver with dual-stream fusion, structure-aware losses are straightforward, flow matching backbone directly borrowed from CellFlow
Performance bounded by quality of pretrained embeddings and pathway databases; limited ablation on these choices (only Figure 5 for embeddings, no sensitivity to PPI threshold)
Inconsistency between claims to move 'beyond static priors' while fundamentally relying on them
Complex pipeline with multiple components (GRC, GCAE, flow matching, two alignment objectives, two-stage training) may hinder adoption and reproducibility
Hyperparameter selections appear somewhat arbitrary (K=32 chosen empirically, λ_corr=λ_pathway=0.1 set equally despite Table 6d showing sensitivity)
Limited analysis of why scBIG wins—unclear which components contribute most to improvements

strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation with 13 baselines, multiple datasets (Norman, RPE1, ComboSciPlex), diverse metrics, and thorough ablations
Biologically well-motivated problem addressing coordinated gene responses at the program level rather than treating genes independently
Good reproducibility with detailed algorithms (1-3), hyperparameter specifications, and promised code release
Solid biological validation through pathway enrichment analysis confirming module coherence
Consistent improvements across all benchmarks (6.7% average over strongest baselines)
Honest discussion of limitations in appendix, including sensitivity to external priors
weaknesses: Limited novelty: Method combines existing techniques (standard OT for clustering, Perceiver architecture, CFM from CellFlow, pathway alignment). Main contribution is integration rather than algorithmic innovation

Fundamental contradiction: Paper criticizes static biological priors for failing to model 'dynamic program reorganization' but proposes static, offline-computed clusters that don't adapt to perturbation conditions. Table 6b shows adaptive clustering actually hurts performance, contradicting core motivation

Modest empirical improvements: 6.7% average gain is incremental for the added complexity. RPE1 gains (25.7% on ρ∆) suggest potential overfitting to Norman dataset. Confidence intervals (Table 15) show overlapping ranges for key ablations

Heavy dependence on external priors without sensitivity analysis: GeneCompass embeddings, STRING PPI threshold (700), Reactome pathways all critical but not analyzed. Switching embeddings changes results substantially (Figure 5), yet no robustness analysis provided

Weak justification for key design choices: K=32 clusters lacks biological justification; balanced constraint is technical convenience, not biological principle; hyperparameters (λ_corr, λ_pathway) appear arbitrary with minimal sensitivity analysis

Limited biological insight: Pathway enrichment only validates modules against known annotations (not discovery); cross-module coordination examples are anecdotal (Table 5); attention shifts (Figure 4) are post-hoc interpretation without demonstrating learned mechanisms

Experimental concerns: CellFlow (bioRxiv 2025) and foundation models not designed for perturbation prediction may not be fair comparisons; ComboSciPlex shows smallest improvements (0.4%); no analysis of failure cases or performance by perturbation type

Presentation issues: 'Code is available at [blank]' indicates incomplete submission; notation inconsistencies; dense paper with unclear component importance; methodology contradicts stated problem formulation

strengths: Well-motivated biological insight: Clear articulation that perturbation responses operate at coordinated program level rather than independent genes, with compelling distinction between gene-wise and module-level views

Comprehensive integrated methodology: Thoughtful three-stage design coherently integrating OT-based clustering, Perceiver-based encoder, and structure-aware alignment with novel biological consistency losses

Rigorous experimental validation: Extensive evaluation across 4 benchmarks, 13 baselines spanning multiple paradigms, 9+ metrics, with particularly impressive OOD improvements (38% on ρ∆D for unseen genes)
Thorough ablation studies: Systematic component ablations (GRC vs K-means: 5.2% improvement), biological loss necessity analysis, embedding comparisons, and hyperparameter sensitivity analysis
Biological validation with interpretability: Functional enrichment alignment with established pathways, perturbation-specific cross-module coordination, mechanistic attention analysis (NOL8→mTORC1)
Statistical rigor: Paired Wilcoxon tests, low standard deviations across 5 seeds, distribution-level metrics, confidence intervals, and qualitative visualizations (density plots)
Reproducibility infrastructure: Detailed algorithms, complete hyperparameter specifications, comprehensive dataset descriptions, promised code release, and honest limitations discussion
weaknesses: Module induction design choices lack principled justification: Balanced cluster constraint is presented as architectural necessity but appears arbitrary; K=32 selection lacks principled criterion beyond sensitivity analysis; static clustering ignores context-dependent program reorganization acknowledged in limitations

Heavy dependence on external priors with limited robustness analysis: Performance depends critically on GeneCompass embeddings and STRING PPI quality; PPI threshold (700) arbitrary with no ablation; unclear how method performs in organisms lacking curated resources

Limited true out-of-distribution evaluation: Norman and RPE1 benchmarks share same protocol/paradigm; cross-cell-line transfer shows modest gains (2.7%); no evaluation on truly novel gene sets or perturbation modalities; claims about OOD generalization may conflate with compositional generalization

Computational scalability concerns: GCAE prohibitively expensive at K=2051 (394 ms/step); two-stage training lengthy without wall-clock comparison to baselines; genome-scale application uncertain per Table 9 scalability analysis

Module validation is partial and somewhat circular: Reactome validation incomplete and creates circularity with pathway-based training loss; perturbation-specific coordination (Table 5) validated on only 3 examples; no comparison to alternative clustering methods (Leiden, spectral, NMF) to validate GRC superiority

Generative modeling choices under-justified: Limited motivation for why conditional flow matching specifically over VAEs or diffusion models; linear interpolation path in Eq. 6 not justified; Sinkhorn regularization ε=1.0 appears arbitrary

Hyperparameter and design choices lack principled justification: λcorr=λpathway=0.1 lacks justification; multiple comparison corrections not discussed; some improvements modest (3.4% ComboSciPlex ρ∆); no analysis of when modular assumptions fail or when gene-wise approaches would be preferable

Limited analysis of methodology vs baselines: Insufficient analysis of why scBIG consistently outperforms CellFlow across metrics; no detailed comparison of complementary strengths; which perturbation types benefit most from modular modeling remains unclear
